_meta.note: Close the last residuals from the v1.27 adversarial review, bump to v1.28, and bring every doc/how-to current with the two prior fix-waves (critical-fixes RV/RB/DC + critical-fixes-2 KB/SP/PT/HN/DR). Three phases. (LK) Write-lock scope honesty — the review's one real residual: tick.sh appends informational events (wake/lease_expired/review_wake/log_event) via raw `>>` OUTSIDE withWlock. That is safe by design (POSIX O_APPEND line writes are atomic; reproject is a full re-fold, so state.json is eventually consistent; the lock only guards the state.json read-modify-write, proven by T139) — but it was undocumented and unproven. Prove it (concurrent appends never corrupt events.jsonl; a non-atomic writer DOES, so the proof has teeth) and document the lock's true scope in parity-notes + dev docs. (GS) git-snapshot parity — the snapshot-on-pass logic is a deliberate cross-runtime pair (bash git_snapshot in gate.sh ≡ python _git_snapshot in gate.py); per the parity contract a shared behavioral surface owes a parity case, and this one had none. Add a behavioral parity proof (a gate pass commits + force-tags the gate id in BOTH runtimes) and note the pair in parity-notes. (VD) Version bump + docs currency — bump plugin/marketplace to 1.28.0 and the Python package to 0.18.0 (independent cadence, already documented as intentional), add the STATUS changelog entry, and sweep dev-plugin.md / dev-python.md / dev-tests.md / parity-notes.md / README so no doc lags the code (review_policy.accept_review as the single review-acceptance source; single-sourced nonBehavioral; coverage floor; tests/fixtures/ paths; withWlock export; gate_blocked breaker; verdict robustness). Gate docs-currency behaviorally: no doc references the moved audit-fixtures/parity-fixtures paths, the review policy is single-sourced, and versions are consistent. Skill-prose commands are kept by decision (no plugin/commands/ dir). Proof-driven throughout: spec-first, lint+audit clean, refuted SOUND, distinct-actor refutation per gate, suites green (node/pytest/parity), commit + tag.

phases.title: Write-lock scope — prove + document that tick.sh's lock-free appends are safe

tasks.title: Spec-first: author the tick-append-safety proof
tasks.description: Author docs/howto/gate-examples/tick-append-safe.sh (a runnable proof). It must (a) fire many concurrent appenders using the EXACT idiom tick.sh uses (echo "{json}" >> "$EVENTS", tick.sh:72/181/338/388) into one events.jsonl and assert every line is valid JSON, no line is torn/interleaved, and all appended ids are present; (b) additionally run several real `bash tick.sh` processes concurrently against one bootstrapped project and assert events.jsonl stays all-valid-JSON; (c) carry a --selftest that swaps the atomic `>>` append for a non-atomic read-concat-write and shows it loses or corrupts updates (proving the proof has teeth). Print TICK-APPEND-SAFE-OK only when every claim holds. Deterministic, self-contained (own mktemp dir), under 5s.

tasks.title: Document the write-lock's true scope
tasks.description: Update planning/parity-notes.md (and a line in docs/dev-plugin.md + docs/dev-python.md) to state the write-lock's real scope: withWlock/with_wlock guards the state.json read-modify-write (mutate = append_event → reproject → atomic write); the append-only informational events tick.sh writes (wake, lease_expired, review_wake, log_event) are intentionally lock-free because O_APPEND line writes are atomic and reproject is a full re-fold, so state.json is eventually consistent. Cite the proof (tick-append-safe.sh) and T139 (the RMW-serialization proof). No overclaim.

tasks.title: Wire the proof into the suite + dev-tests
tasks.description: Wire tick-append-safe.sh into tests/run-tests.sh as a new T-group (run the proof, grep its TICK-APPEND-SAFE-OK marker on the same line) and add the matching row to docs/dev-tests.md (T124 anti-drift requires the enumeration stays current).

phases.title: git-snapshot parity — the cross-runtime snapshot pair gets a parity case

tasks.title: Spec-first: author the git-snapshot parity proof
tasks.description: Author docs/howto/gate-examples/git-snapshot-parity.sh (a runnable proof) that proves gate.sh's bash git_snapshot and gate.py's python _git_snapshot behave identically ON THE PATH HEARTBEAT ACTUALLY USES — the REVIEW-ACCEPTANCE snapshot (real phases are review-gated, so the commit+tag is deferred to `review pass`, gate.sh:154-160 / gate.py:87-90; the on-pass branch only fires for non-review gates). So: in a temp git repo, for EACH runtime, drive a review-gated phase to review acceptance (write a substantive distinct-actor artifact and run `node .hb/hb.js review GATE pass --artifact f` for node / `hb review GATE pass --artifact f` (or review_policy.accept_review) for python with HB_ACTOR set), then assert BOTH runtimes created a commit AND force-created a git tag named exactly after the gate id. The proof MUST contain an internal negative assertion: if either runtime produced no tag, it prints FAIL and exits non-zero (so a silently-skipped snapshot goes RED, not green). Run under `env -u HB_NO_GIT -u HB_NO_HOOK` (the suite exports both). Print GIT-SNAPSHOT-PARITY-OK only when both runtimes tagged at review acceptance. Deterministic, self-contained (own mktemp git repo), under 5s.

tasks.title: Wire the parity proof + note the pair
tasks.description: Wire git-snapshot-parity.sh into tests/run-tests.sh as a new T-group (run + grep GIT-SNAPSHOT-PARITY-OK on the same line) and add the docs/dev-tests.md row. Add a line to planning/parity-notes.md recording that git-snapshot is a deliberate cross-runtime behavioral pair (bash git_snapshot in gate.sh ≡ python _git_snapshot in gate.py) — cannot be code-shared across languages, so it is held by this parity proof.

GATE_LK.desc: tick.sh's lock-free appends are proven safe under concurrency and the lock's true scope is documented — no overclaim, real teeth.

review.prompt: Refute that LK is done. Does tick-append-safe.sh actually prove O_APPEND atomicity — i.e. does its --selftest non-atomic writer genuinely go RED (lost/torn updates), and does the real path stay green across repeated runs (not flaky)? Does it exercise the REAL tick.sh append idiom (and real concurrent `bash tick.sh`), not a strawman? Do parity-notes + dev docs state the lock's scope honestly (guards the state.json RMW; informational appends are lock-free by design) without overclaiming that all writes are locked? Is the proof wired by running it and asserting its marker, not by grepping a filename? node/python/parity green?

criteria.desc: parity-notes documents the write-lock's true scope by EXPLAINING THE MECHANISM (not just a token): lock-free/atomic appends + reproject re-fold + events.jsonl must co-occur — a contradicting/opposite doc lacks all three
criteria.cmd: cd "$PROJECT_DIR" && grep -qiE 'lock-free|O_APPEND|atomic append|atomic.*append' planning/parity-notes.md && grep -qiE 'reproject|re-fold|full fold|full re-fold' planning/parity-notes.md && grep -qi 'events.jsonl' planning/parity-notes.md

criteria.desc: the proof is wired into the suite and enumerated in dev-tests
